A long horizon of cobalt and crimson bead-dabs crosses the full width as the anchor, splitting two soft fields. Above, a pale pink column and an ochre-cored green bar drift apart through open cream, and a dappled cornflower cloud breathes at the right edge. Below, a lone cobalt spool floats in rose wash. Feathered, bleeding edges, thin translucent oil, diffuse sourceless glow, quiet hush.

Do not start by duplicating the original source framing and object layout. Start from the strongest borrowed source elements, then recompose them through split-field multiform drift around a horizon band / frontal flat plate, full-bleed painted surface, no perspective. full-width bead-dab horizon dividing two airy fields; upper pink column and green-ochre bar pushed apart across open cream.
ANCHORS
Compose exactly 1 distinct source-native physical feature within the artwork: Full-width horizon of alternating cobalt and crimson bead-dabs. Keep it large and visibly separable; never a counted symbol, card, pasted thumbnail or UI label. No painted indicators. No visible annotation glyphs or QA chrome. No registration targets, crosshairs, reticles or hollow target rings.

even, diffuse, sourceless glow emanating from the color fields themselves; materials: thinned oil wash on raw linen; stained cream gesso ground; scumbled translucent pigment; dappled dry-brush blue; palette: cream-dominant with rose pinks, cobalt blues, crimson accents, and one teal-ochre ember.
